surface.product: Vista Cloud Digital Platform, Omni-Channel API (OCAPI)

behaviour.summary: Explicit cancellation is documented as recommended rather than required, and the reason given is that it releases seats immediately rather than waiting for background processes which may take a few minutes. Release after abandonment is therefore eventually consistent, on an unstated bound, at the operator's own admission.
behaviour.testable_as: Abandon an order without cancelling and measure the interval until the seats become available to a second caller. The vendor states this is minutes; no bound is published.
behaviour.consequence_for_agents: Seats that no one holds still read as unavailable for an unstated interval, so an agent cannot distinguish a full house from a lagging sweeper, and neither can the exhibitor's own conversion numbers. CHANGEOVER makes release total and explicit, and C-RELEASE asserts seats are re-holdable within a MEASURED bound rather than a described one.

half_life_basis: A claim about internal timing that no external party can check, on a page the vendor maintains. Believed on the vendor's authority alone, so it decays faster than a contract statement: four months.

citation.quote: This will ensure seats are released immediately rather than waiting for background processes which may take a few minutes.

verification_gap: A few minutes is not a number. Turning this into a measurement needs tenant access and two callers, and the resulting series — real release latency at a real boundary — is exactly what nobody in this industry publishes.
